## 1. Bounded dedup and fixed scope

The old source theorem 323515c8... and adjoint paper 960557fe... already
give L_old H=0, M=L_old composed with multiplication by(x-1), the complete
forcing, and the standard flat Green product rule. Here L=-L_old, so the

The reciprocal-half paper already gives H(1/2)=0 and
V=E T=(1-g-H+g x^N)/(1-x). These are reused, not re-proved as new
mathematical achievements. The saved Gauss paper already gives the
inhomogeneous equation for the prescribed arithmetic lift; the new
harmonic certificate specifies all of that lift's coefficients.

Bounded text/section checks of the source, adjoint, reciprocal-half,
canonical finite-transpose, two source/endpoint transport, and
Gauss-weighted-telescoper papers did not find the particular
x^N(1-x)-weighted conjugation or the source-generated boundary and
resonant pairings developed here. The old transport's different flat
gauge and resonant projection are not rerun. This is a scoped overlap
check, not a global absence or novelty claim; no nested actual-response
archives or old sample/checker were read or executed.

Keep the ORIGINAL prime family p=13 or19 modulo24, p=6m+1, m>=2,
N=3m=(p-1)/2 as a literal integer, c=1/2, c^N=-1, g a unit,
s=1-2g possibly zero. All calculations below are in F_p[x] or explicitly
in F_p(x); N=-1/2 is used only in derivative coefficients.

Let H=h(rho(x)), DeltaH=Delta(rho(x)), rho=x(4x-3)^2.
The prescribed h and Delta are the full terminating source and its
p-integral normalized difference; division byp preceded reduction.
Their retained data are

    degH=N, H(0)=g, [x^N]H=g, H(1)=1, H(c)=0;
    degDeltaH<=N, DeltaH(0)=delta_g,
    [x^N]DeltaH=delta_ell, DeltaH(1)=0.

Neither delta scalar is assumed nonzero. Set D=d/dx and

    A=2x(1-x)(4x-1),
    B=-20x^2+15x-1, C=1-4x,
    L=A D^2+B D+C, w=x^N(1-x),

    M=2x(1-x)^2(4x-1)D^2
       +(1-x)(-36x^2+19x-1)D+2(12x^2-10x+1).

The actual polynomial V=E T has degree<=N-2, V(0)=s, and satisfies
the COMPLETE source equation

    M V=F=(1-g)(1-4x)-g(1-x)x^(N-1),                  (1)

## 2. Exact polynomial Gauss pullback, including all critical factors

Write dot for the derivative in the external Gauss argument z. The
saved source operators are

    L0=z(1-z)D_z^2+(1/2-3z/2)D_z-1/18,
    R0=(1-z)D_z-1/6,

    L0 h=0, L0 Delta=-R0 h.                           (3)

The full elementary identities are

    rho'=3(4x-3)(4x-1), rho''=48(2x-1),
    1-rho=(1-x)(4x-1)^2.

For ANY polynomial f(z), the three coefficients after applying L to
f(rho) are checked separately:

    A(rho')^2=18(4x-1)rho(1-rho),
    A rho''+B rho'=9(4x-1)(1-3rho),
    C=18(4x-1)(-1/18).

For the middle equality one may factor 3(4x-1); its remaining polynomial
is

    32x(1-x)(2x-1)+B(4x-3)=3(1-3rho).

Thus, without dividing by rho' at a critical point,

    L[f(rho)]=18(4x-1)(L0 f)(rho)                    (4)

as an exact polynomial identity. This verifies L H=0 with the fixed
normalization and all degree terms; the underlying homogeneous
source fact itself was already known.

Define the actual inhomogeneous polynomial J=L DeltaH. Equations
(3)-(4), with their sign retained, give

    J=3(4x-1)H-18(1-x)(4x-1)^3 dot h(rho).            (5)

Equivalently in F_p(x),

    J=3(4x-1)H
          -6(1-x)(4x-1)^2 H'/(4x-3).                (6)

The apparent pole in (6) is removable for THIS actual source:
H'=3(4x-3)(4x-1)dot h(rho). Equation (5) is the polynomial expression
to use at x=3/4, at other critical points and at all endpoints. No
regularity assumption about an arbitrary polynomial is substituted.

There is a stronger literal degree check than a raw expanded bound.
If h has leading z coefficient q_m, the coefficient of z^m in R0 h
is -(m+1/6)q_m=0 in F_p. Thus deg(R0 h)<=m-1 while m remains the
integer termination bound. Consequently

    degJ<=3(m-1)+1=N-2.                              (7)

No term has been dropped: the nominal high term cancels by 6m+1=p
in its coefficient. We do not replace an exponent by -1/6.

At the origin q_1=g/9 follows from the original Gauss coefficients.
Equation (5) then gives

    J(0)=-3g+18q_1=-g.                              (8)

This also follows from J(0)=DeltaH(0)-DeltaH'(0). It will be retained
in the finite resonance calculation.

## 3. All three coefficients of the weighted formal adjoint

The flat formal adjoint is

    L*=A D^2+(2A'-B)D+(A''-B'+C),
    2A'-B=-28x^2+25x-3,
    A''-B'+C=6-12x.

The literal polynomial w has logarithmic derivative and second ratio

    w'/w=N/x-1/(1-x),
    w''/w=N(N-1)/x^2-2N/[x(1-x)].

Reducing ONLY these scalar N coefficients gives

    lambda=w'/w=-1/(2x)-1/(1-x),
    w''/w=3/(4x^2)+1/[x(1-x)].

We now check the conjugated operator on ALL coefficients.

Second derivative:

    (1-x)A=2x(1-x)^2(4x-1).

First derivative:

    2A lambda=-8x^2-6x+2,

so

    (1-x)[2A lambda+2A'-B]
       =(1-x)(-36x^2+19x-1).

Zeroth derivative: put Bstar=2A'-B. Directly,

    A(w''/w)+Bstar lambda+(6-12x)
       =(4x-1)-Bstar/(1-x).

Multiplying by(1-x) gives

    (1-x)(4x-1)-Bstar=24x^2-20x+2.

These are precisely the three coefficients of M. Therefore

    M=(1-x)w^(-1) L* composed with multiplication byw (9)

in F_p(x), with all tails and zeroth-order terms included. The more
useful polynomial form, avoiding division at0 or1, is

    L*(w V)=x^N M V                                  (10)

for every polynomial V. Both sides are genuine polynomials. The rational
coefficient calculation establishes (10) identically, so it remains
valid at the zeros of w; singular individual terms are never evaluated.

For reference, combining (9) with the old M=L composed with
multiplication by(1-x) gives the source-generated adjoint kernel

    L*(x^N H)=x^N L H=0.                              (11)

Here one may apply the established rational operator identity to
H/(1-x), after which the resulting expression x^N H is polynomial.
This is not a homogeneous-adjoint certificate for the target row(5,3).

## 4. Full Green identity and actual polynomial boundary rows

For arbitrary polynomials f,V define y=wV and the COMPLETE concomitant

    G_f,V=A(f y'-f' y)+(A'-B)f y.

The product rule gives

    G_f,V'=f L*y-y Lf
           =x^N f M V-w V Lf.                       (12)

This is the standard flat Green rule with the NEW specified weight;
the generic product rule itself was already saved.

Using A'-B=(1-x)(4x-1) and the actual derivative of w, the whole
concomitant factors as a polynomial:

    G_f,V=2x^(N+1)(1-x)(4x-1)
             [(1-x)(f V'-f' V)-f V].                (13)

In particular the complete values at0 and1 are BOTH zero. This remains
true when f(0) or V(1) is nonzero; it follows from the factored whole
polynomial, not from separately evaluating a singular logarithmic
derivative. At c use c^N=-1 only after the integer polynomial is fixed:

    G_f,V(c)=f(c)V(c)/2-f(c)V'(c)/4+f'(c)V(c)/4.       (14)

There is no division by f, f', s or an endpoint value.

For the actual V in (1), the two source pairings are

    G_H,V'=R_H=x^N H F,                              (15)

    G_DeltaH,V'=R_Delta=x^N DeltaH F-w V J.           (16)

All forcing terms of J and F are retained. Their half-point values are
especially informative about scope. Equation (2) and H(c)=0 give

    V(c)=2s,
    V'(c)=4s+2g-2H'(c).

Substituting into(14), without using an actual T boundary, yields

    G_H,V(c)=s H'(c)/2,                              (17)

    G_DeltaH,V(c)
       =[DeltaH(c)(H'(c)-g)+s DeltaH'(c)]/2.          (18)

Thus the first Green row collapses to already source-known data; the
second is a specified arithmetic-source half-period combination. Neither
row is the target 5T(c)+3T'(c). Passing from M to V=E T does not justify
replacing it by a first-jet row of T.

## 5. The characteristic-p resonant coefficient, computed explicitly

If d=degf<=N and v=degV<=N-2, (13) has degree at most

    N+3+d+v<=3N+1.

Both RHS polynomials in(15)-(16) have degree at most3N: for (16),
the second term has degree at most(N+1)+(N-2)+(N-2)=3N-3 by(7).

As p-1=2N and3N<2p-1, precisely ONE possible derivative obstruction
occurs in this range. For every polynomial Q,

    [x^(p-1)]Q'=0,

since the only contributing term would be x^p and its derivative
coefficient is p=0. Applying this to the complete Green identities
is a finite coefficient pairing, not ordinary definite integration.

Write h_j=[x^j]H, delta_j=[x^j]DeltaH. The source pullback and the full
finite harmonic certificate give the following FOUR edge relations:

    h_1=h_0=g, h_(N-1)=g/4,
    delta_1-delta_0=g, delta_(N-1)=delta_N/4.          (19)

For clarity, h_1=9q_1=g. The top two coefficients come only from
rho^m=16^m x^N[1-3/(2x)+9/(16x^2)]^m, whose next coefficient is
-3m/2=1/4 in F_p; this argument also holds if delta_N=0. For the
delta low relation, the all-k certificate gives
delta_1=g(chi+S_1), delta_0=g chi and S_1=1/b-1/c=1
with b=1/3,c=1/2 after reduction. No division by a delta scalar is used.

For (15), the full resonant coefficient is

    [x^(2N)]R_H
       =(1-g)(h_N-4h_(N-1))-g(h_1-h_0)=0.            (20)

Both the low and high pieces of F occur here; dropping either forcing
monomial would not be the prescribed pairing.

For(16), the FIRST term has coefficient

    [x^(2N)]x^N DeltaH F
       =(1-g)(delta_N-4delta_(N-1))
                      -g(delta_1-delta_0)
       =-g^2.

Consequently the exact resonant compatibility condition is

    [x^N](1-x)V J=-g^2.                              (21)

Using the COMPLETE source relation(2), degJ<=N-2 and J(0)=-g,
equation(21) is equivalently the source-only finite pairing

    [x^N]H J=0,    J=L DeltaH.                       (22)

No unknown boundary occurs in(21)-(22).

There is also a direct consistency proof of(22). The canonical flat
concomitant for L satisfies
D C_L(u,f)=u Lf-f L*u. Put u=x^N H and f=DeltaH; equation(11) gives
D C_L=x^N H J. Its degree permits the same x^(p-1) coefficient test,

## 6. Retaining and fixing the literal x^p kernel

A derivative identity alone does NOT fix the half-point value. In the
present literal degree bound, the polynomial derivative kernel is

    {a+b x^p : a,b in F_p},

because3N+1<2p. In particular it is incorrect to discard the x^p term
or pretend the entire Green polynomial has degree below p.

There is, however, a precise finite transgression with BOTH complete
boundary values. For either R=R_H or R_Delta, the resonance at p-1
vanishes by the proven identities. Define the finite coefficient right
inverse with the resonant slot omitted,

    P_R(x)=sum_{0<=j<=3N, j!=p-1} R_j x^(j+1)/(j+1),
    R_j=[x^j]R.                                     (23)

Every displayed denominator is a unit: the only multiple of p among
1,...,3N+1 is p itself, and its slot is omitted only after R_(p-1)=0
has been proved. Integer exponents j+1, including those above p,
are retained. This is an algebraic coefficient map, not an analytic
integral or a new dense inverse defining T.

Then P_R'=R, P_R(0)=0, and its x^p coefficient is zero by definition.
Thus from G'=R and the degree bound,

    G=P_R+a+b x^p.

The genuine polynomial boundary G(0)=0 forces a=0. The genuine
boundary G(1)=0 then forces b=-P_R(1). Hence the FULL relation is

    G(x)=P_R(x)-x^p P_R(1),                          (24)

and at the field point c,

    G(c)=P_R(c)-c P_R(1).                            (25)

The kernel coefficient is therefore NOT assumed zero: it is fixed
to -P_R(1) by the second endpoint. Keeping only G(0)=0 would leave
it undetermined. Equations(24)-(25) are valid in every original field,
with no additional small-prime case or rank transport.

Combining(17)-(18) with(25) gives explicit finite source pairings

    P_RH(c)-c P_RH(1)=s H'(c)/2,

    P_RDelta(c)-c P_RDelta(1)
       =[DeltaH(c)(H'(c)-g)+s DeltaH'(c)]/2.          (26)

These retain the high-degree coefficient pairing and the Frobenius
correction. They do not evaluate or silently remove it. A claim that an
ordinary 0-to-c primitive alone equals the Green boundary would omit
the term -c P_R(1) and would be unjustified.
